column1: # THE REPAIR STRIDE -- PO-78's repair phase.  Set at r7329, re-cut to two seats at r7331, re-cut to
#   THREE SEATS at r7339 when the secondment's return trigger fired.  Data, not code.
# ** THIS IS THE WHOLE LIST AND IT IS NOT A TRIAGE. **  Every REPAIR-OWED row in
#   corpus/quote_pin_baseline.tsv is on it.  AT r7341: 268 rows in 82 receipts over 53 prefixes,
#   down from 366 in 135 at r7329.  A row leaves by being REPAIRED or by being WITHDRAWN with its case
#   written down beside the repair -- never by reclassification and never by looking hard at it.
#   Median 3 rows a receipt, mean 3.27, max 12; 10 of the 82 receipts hold exactly one.
#   The whole list splits 155 PAPER / 113 SOURCE and 177 SENTENCE / 91 TOKEN.
# ** THE UNIT IS THE RECEIPT, NOT THE ROW, AND THE BALANCE IS ON RECEIPTS. **  A repair edits a receipt's
#   assertions, so a receipt holding five owed rows is one repair touching five keys.  r7329's first cut
#   balanced on ROWS and came out 74 receipts against 61 -- balancing on the wrong unit, caught in the
#   same cycle.  r7339's three-seat cut was 30 receipts a seat exactly.  NO RE-CUT AT r7341: cc66 has
#   worked 8 receipts off its 30 and is simply ahead, which is the cut doing its job rather than failing.
#   A re-cut comes when a seat runs dry, not when the counts stop being equal.
# ** THREE SEATS.  THE SECONDMENT IS DISCHARGED (r7339). **  70 returned when 71's census read
#   REOPENABLE 0.  70 keeps the nightly at 11:00 UTC.  Node 71 is not on this stride -- it has the Lean
#   census and the campaigns.  Node 69 is not a workhorse and takes none.
# ** THE RE-CUT RULE, FROM r7333. **  A stride re-cut applies to work NOT YET BEGUN, and the blocks a
#   seat was told to do FIRST under the old cut stay that seat's.  r7331 reassigned L147_two_arm to 60
#   while 70 was already working it under r7329's order; both seats repaired the same 13 rows.
# ** AFFINITY. **  cc66 holds P15_CR_cosmology and its own sector prefixes; 60 holds the
#   L165/L175/L211/L204 block it verdicted; 70's 30 are the tail that had not been begun at r7339.
# ** WHAT A REPAIR IS. **  THE_RULE.md at 1a3c13a61 is the WORKING RULE, adopted at r7329 and refined in
#   use, now carrying two amendments.  A repair makes the check assert what the claim IS rather than that
#   a sentence is present.  Where the rule owes a repair that should not be owed, or misses one it should
#   catch, the case is written down beside the repair and the rule is amended from those cases in small
#   named changes.  The text stays applied throughout.
# ** AND NO INTER-RATER MEASURE GOVERNS A REPAIR (r7333). **  Two independent repairs of the same 13 rows
#   passed all five receipts while agreeing on 48-78 per cent of what to remove: a repair has many correct
#   outputs where a verdict had one.
# ** THE ARBITER, RESTATED AT r7341 BECAUSE THE OLD STATEMENT OF IT WAS A COUNT. **  It is
#   `bash scripts/sweep_gates.sh` plus the carry ledger
#   (git fetch origin refs/ci/carry && git show FETCH_HEAD:carry.json), per repair.  This header said
#   "the 134-gate sweep" for four revisions and there are 129 gate files -- a count cited where a roster
#   was meant, which is cc66's own r7339+cc66.2 lesson landing on the document that names the arbiter.
#   ⛔ cc66 ran the sweep as `while read g; do ... done < gatelist.txt` and a gate's child consumed the
#   rest of the list, because the list IS the loop's stdin: it wrote DONE having recorded 120 of the 134
#   it claimed, the 13 missing being exactly the tail, check_revision_collisions among them.
#   ⇒ FIXED AT r7341 IN scripts/sweep_gates.sh, structurally and not by advice: every gate is invoked
#   with `< /dev/null`, and the sweep ASSERTS ITS OWN ROSTER -- it records each name it runs and goes red
#   if that set is not exactly the set of gate files.  A tally that cannot be reconciled is not a result.
#   ** No seat runs an ad-hoc gate loop any more.  Run the script. **
# ** AND TWO QUANTITIES, NEITHER STANDING FOR THE OTHER (r7333, r7337). **  Report EFFORT and REALISED
#   receipts a revision with the assignment named; and report the owed count BESIDE the keys minted and
#   adjudicated.  AT r7341 the second quantity has its first trunk-wide measurement: 24 keys minted and
#   adjudicated against 16 rows cleared, 1.50 a row, against 0.30 the revision before.
# ** WHAT A REPAIR WRITES: TWO AMENDMENTS, AND THE SECOND IS CORRECTED THE REVISION IT LANDED. **
#   THE_RULE.md (r7335, 69 from 60's case): the shortest span that carries the whole claim and occurs once
#   under the checker's own normalisation, then stop.  (r7339/r7341, 69 from cc66's case): a pin may be
#   SEVERAL spans required together inside ONE LOCUS -- one anchor occurring exactly once, every other
#   span required within the anchor's locus, exactly one locus holding them all.  A pin none of whose
#   spans occurs once has nothing to locate it and does not meet the floor however its pieces are
#   arranged.  Counts are taken normalised, because the normaliser only merges and a raw count is a lower
#   bound.
#   ⛔ AND THE MINIMAND IS CORRECTED AT r7341, AGAINST THE GATE'S OWN r7339 RULING.  r7339 set the
#   minimand to total pinned characters and told cc66 to prefer the locus-scoped form.  Measured on the
#   trunk: the locus-scoped form minted 0 keys of 7 repairs at r7335, and the contiguous form minted 24
#   against 16 rows cleared at r7341.  A pin the instrument cannot key is not a cheaper pin; it is not on
#   the minimand's domain.  ⇒ THE MINIMAND RANKS PINS THE RATCHET CAN READ.  Among keyable pins, fewest
#   pinned characters over all spans.  When cc66's narrowed hop lands and the locus-scoped form becomes
#   keyable, the minimand will prefer it with no further change -- the domain widens when the instrument
#   widens, which is why this is not a sunset clause.
#   ⌗ And contiguity's price is now measured from both ends on the same eight rows: uniqueness alone
#   0.60x the locus-scoped form, uniqueness-plus-contiguity 2.81x (410 characters -> 1154).  cc66's
#   earlier 10.3x measured the anchor SENTENCE, which the rule never asks for, and cc66 withdrew it.
# ** FLOOR 2 DOES NOT APPLY TO A PINNED CONTAINER (r7341, cc66's case and cc66's reason). **  The defect
#   floor 2 prevents is a later edit landing on the wrong site; a container pinned at a commit has no
#   later edits.  Rows asserted against a frozen file are not owed a uniqueness repair.
# ** AND TWO CLASSES THE OWED COUNT CANNOT SEE, ROUTED TO cc66 WITH THE NARROWED HOP (r7341). **
#   ⒜ THE DEAD PIN: cc66 found a disjunction whose STRONGER arm matches zero times, so the check had been
#   passing on the weaker arm alone -- and the dead arm carried a ledger row, verdict EXTENDED, green.
#   A pin that matches nothing can sit adjudicated indefinitely because the disjunction around it carries
#   the check, and no count of owed rows can see it.
#   ⒝ THE VANISHING SPAN: 15 of 302 P15-wide readings vanish under the normaliser entirely, every one
#   produced by EXTENDING a shorter literal by a character distance so the boundary lands mid-token.
#   Neither class is a repair and neither is on the list below; both are measurements the ledger owes
#   itself, because they decide whether a falling owed count means anything.
